threads.body: The PR description and comments indicate this workflow is for issues awaiting author feedback, but the job is also granted `pull-requests: write` and configures `stale-pr-*` messages/labels, so it will operate on PRs with the label as well. Either restrict the stale action to issues only (and drop PR permissions/messages) or update the PR/workflow docs to explicitly state PRs are included.
threads.hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+name: Issue management - run stale action
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    # daily at 09:47 UTC
+    - cron: "47 9 * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  stale:
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      actions: write # because actions/stale deletes its old cache before saving new one
+      issues: write  # for actions/stale to close stale issues
+      pull-requests: write  # for actions/stale to close stale PRs

threads.body: `pull-requests: write` looks unnecessary here: the workflow only runs `gh issue edit` to remove labels, and label edits for PRs also go through the Issues API. Consider dropping `pull-requests: write` to follow least-privilege permissions.

threads.body: This scheduled workflow can be triggered both by `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` but has no `concurrency` guard. Adding a concurrency group helps prevent overlapping runs that could double-comment/close or contend on the stale action cache.
threads.hunk:

threads.body: The `actions/checkout` step isn’t used by any subsequent step (the workflow only calls `gh issue edit`). Removing it will reduce runtime and token surface area.
threads.hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+name: Issue management - remove labels as needed
+
+on:
+  issue_comment:
+    types: [created]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read

+      pull-requests: write
+    if: >

+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:

+
+      - name: Remove labels

threads.body: `concurrency` block indentation is inconsistent with the rest of this repo’s workflow YAMLs (they use 2-space indentation). While YAML will likely still parse, aligning indentation improves readability and avoids style churn in future edits.
